# RUNTIME dependencies use ranges, because this is a published library.
#
# An exact pin here is not caution, it is a conflict: it forces every app that
# uses this package onto that exact version, and any other package asking for
# `crypto ^3.0.7` makes the whole thing unresolvable. pub.dev warns about it for
# that reason.
#
# The pinning discipline still applies -- it just belongs one level up. Apps
# commit a lockfile, so a deliberate bump across all eight beats an accidental
# one in whichever app happened to be rebuilt. Dev dependencies below stay
# pinned: they constrain nobody but this repository's own CI.
dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  crypto: ^3.0.6
  # The device token is an identity and belongs in the Keystore. The cached
  # entitlement ANSWER is not a credential and stays in plain preferences.
  #
  # 10.x, and NOT 9.x, because 9.x makes this package unresolvable in any app
  # that also has `package_info_plus`:
  #
  #   package_info_plus ^10.2.1 -> win32 ^6.0.1
  #   flutter_secure_storage ^9.2.4
  #     -> flutter_secure_storage_windows ^3.1.2 -> win32 ^5.0.0
  #
  # Windows is not a platform any ACKBiz app ships, and the conflict still
  # blocks `flutter pub get` outright -- pub resolves every platform's
  # dependencies whether or not you build for it. 10.x takes
  # flutter_secure_storage_windows ^4.2.x, which is on win32 ^6.
  #
  # NOT ^11.0.0, and this is the part to read before widening it: v11 requires
  # compileSdk 37, so taking it means moving every consuming app's Android
  # build up, not just this constraint. The code here works unchanged on both
  # -- `const AndroidOptions()` is identical in 10 and 11 -- so this becomes a
  # one-line change on the day the fleet is on 37, and should not happen
  # before then.
  flutter_secure_storage: ^10.3.1
  # NOT android_id: the plugin already reads Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID over
  # its own channel, so a second dependency for one string buys nothing.
  #
  # The alternative rail's checkout IS this package's job: create the order,
  # open the sheet, poll for the outcome, map the status. That sequence is easy
  # to get wrong and expensive when it is, so it lives in one place.
  # For `package:ackbiz_billing/http.dart` ONLY -- a separate entry point, so
  # an app that implements the seam itself imports none of it. `http` is small,
  # stable and already in most Flutter trees, which is what makes a ready-made
  # sender cheaper than eight apps each re-deriving the return-vs-throw rule.
  http: ^1.2.0
  razorpay_flutter: ^1.4.0
  # For the offline entitlement answer, which is a decision and not a
  # credential -- the token is what needs the Keystore.
  shared_preferences: ^2.3.3
  #
  # NOT purchases_flutter, deliberately. `Entitlements` already takes
  # RevenueCat as an injected `Future<bool> Function()`, so wiring it is three
  # lines in an app that has the SDK anyway for its paywall. Depending on it
  # here would buy those three lines and cost all eight apps a forced version
  # constraint on a heavy native SDK they already manage themselves.

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_lints: 5.0.0

# The Android plugin.
#
# This block was removed once, deliberately: it named `AckBizBillingPlugin` as
# an entry point that did not exist, with no android/build.gradle and no
# manifest behind it -- so every app adding this package failed its Gradle sync
# on a native module that cannot compile. `pub publish` does not catch that; it
# validates metadata and archive shape, not whether a plugin builds.
#
# It is back because the module is: build.gradle, manifest, the plugin class,
# and UcbBillingManager behind it, compiled against Play Billing 7.
#
# ANDROID ONLY, and honestly so. Alternative billing is a Play programme and
# the backend is Android-only by scope (Q8). Listing ios: here would make the
# package look cross-platform and fail at runtime on the first call.
flutter:
  plugin:
    platforms:
      android:
        package: com.ackbiz.billing
        pluginClass: AckBizBillingPlugin

pubspec_yaml:
name: adaptive_app_icon
description: >-
  Switch your app's home-screen icon at runtime between pre-bundled variants,
  with a config-driven codegen system and a drop-in icon gallery widget.
version: 0.1.0
homepage: https://github.com/Dsoji/adaptive_app_icon
repository: https://github.com/Dsoji/adaptive_app_icon
issue_tracker: https://github.com/Dsoji/adaptive_app_icon/issues
topics:
  - icons
  - app-icon
  - launcher
  - ios
  - android

environment:
  sdk: ^3.11.5
  flutter: '>=3.3.0'

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  # Runtime: local cache of the selected icon so the UI doesn't flash the
  # default on cold start before the native call resolves.
  shared_preferences: ^2.3.0
  # Used by the `generate_icon_config` executable (bin/). These are pure-Dart
  # and must be regular dependencies so consumers can run the codegen via
  # `dart run adaptive_app_icon:generate_icon_config`.
  yaml: ^3.1.2
  xml: ^7.0.1
  path: ^1.9.0
  # Build-time only: renders the Android density PNGs and iOS app-icon sets from
  # each icon's single source image. Never imported by runtime code, so it is
  # tree-shaken out of your app binary.
  image: ^4.9.1

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_lints: ^6.0.0
  # Type-safe Dart <-> Swift/Kotlin bindings. Run with:
  #   dart run pigeon --input pigeons/messages.dart
  pigeon: ^22.0.0

# The following section is specific to Flutter packages.
flutter:
  plugin:
    platforms:
      android:
        package: com.sojku.adaptive_app_icon
        pluginClass: DynamicAppIconPlugin
      ios:
        pluginClass: DynamicAppIconPlugin

Human approval before a tool that changes something runs, showing the exact arguments the model proposed and that the tool is not read-only.
The trace inspector: every event the run published, correlated by run and trace id, on the device rather than in a log somewhere else.
